performers: John Harrison, violin; Wichita State University Chamber Players; Robert Turizziani, conductor
intro: The third movement, Allegro, of Winter, RV 297, from Vivaldi’s The Four Seasons opens with the solo violin on the ice over a long held F in the bass, and soon all the players are slipping. The concerto ends with the Sirocco and the north wind fighting through the strings.

sections.label: A · Solo violin over F pedal
sections.mNote: The solo violin plays above a sustained F in the bass.

sections.label: B · Strings over C, descending figures
sections.mNote: The strings enter over C and play descending figures.

sections.label: C · Solo semiquavers over held strings
sections.mNote: The solo violin climbs in detached semiquavers above held strings.

sections.label: D · Short string phrases, C minor
sections.mNote: Short string phrases separate into fragments in C minor.

sections.label: E · Lento, E♭ major, without basses
sections.mNote: Lento in E♭ major; the low strings rest.

sections.label: F · Solo runs and repeated-note tutti
sections.mNote: Solo runs alternate with repeated-note passages for the orchestra.

sections.label: F′ · Wind figures in F minor
sections.mNote: The full strings play the wind figures to the cadence.

cues.title: Winter sonnet, letters F–G
cues.text: “Caminar Sopra’l giaccio, e à passo lento / Per timor di cader gersene intenti”, “To walk on ice with slow steps, taking care for fear of falling”, come from the 1725 Winter sonnet. The solo violin changes direction above a long F. The other upper strings rest.
cues.evidence: Winter sonnet, letters F–G; translation ours. Mutopia score after Performers’ Facsimiles, III, bars 1–20: https://www.mutopiaproject.org/cgibin/piece-info.cgi?id=351. The sonnets were published anonymously with Op. 8.
cues.how: Timed from the score, aligned to this recording automatically.

cues.title: Falling and running on the ice
cues.text: “Gir forte Sdruzziolar, cader à terra / Di nuovo ir Sopra ’l giaccio e correr forte” — “Turn sharply, slip, fall to the ground; go back onto the ice and run hard.” The orchestra plays falling scales. Then the solo violin climbs in detached semiquavers.
cues.evidence: Winter sonnet, 1725, letters H–I; translation ours. Mutopia score, III, bars 40–60, including Cader à terra at bar 48 and Correr forte at bar 51: https://www.mutopiaproject.org/cgibin/piece-info.cgi?id=351.
cues.how: Timed from the score, aligned to this recording automatically.

cues.title: Sonnet line L, the ice breaking
cues.text: “Sin ch’il giaccio Si rompe, e Si disserra” — “Until the ice breaks and splits open.” The strings break off their running figures with short notes and rests. Brief bursts of demisemiquavers fill the gaps, and then the soloist takes over again.
cues.evidence: Winter sonnet, 1725, letter L; translation ours. Mutopia score, III, bars 85–100, especially the rests and short figures at bars 89–92: https://www.mutopiaproject.org/cgibin/piece-info.cgi?id=351.
cues.how: Timed from the score, aligned to this recording automatically.

cues.title: Sirocco episode, Lento
cues.text: “Sentir uscir dalle ferrate porte” — “To hear emerging from the iron gates.” The sonnet describes the winds. For the Sirocco, Vivaldi marked the music Lento in E♭ major and left out the bass entirely, so only the upper strings play.
cues.evidence: Winter sonnet, 1725, letter M; translation ours. Mutopia score, III, bars 101–119, marked Il Vento Sirocco and Lento, with basso tacet: https://www.mutopiaproject.org/cgibin/piece-info.cgi?id=351.
cues.how: Timed from the score, aligned to this recording automatically.

cues.title: Closing section, sonnet letter N
cues.text: “Sirocco, Borea, e tutti i Venti in guerra” — “Sirocco, Boreas, and all the winds at war.” Solo runs alternate with short orchestral passages, and the strings move towards F minor. The sonnet ends: “Quest’è ’l verno, mà tal, che gioja apporte” — “This is winter, yet it brings joy.”
cues.evidence: Winter sonnet, 1725, letter N and final line; translation ours. Mutopia score, III, bars 120–153; the last line is printed above the closing bars: https://www.mutopiaproject.org/cgibin/piece-info.cgi?id=351.
cues.how: Timed from the score, aligned to this recording automatically.

transitions.title: The bass pedal moves from F to C
transitions.from: A · Solo violin over F pedal
transitions.to: B · Strings over C, descending figures
transitions.how: The bass moves from its held F to C, the dominant of F minor. The orchestral strings join the soloist, first in running semiquavers and then in quavers. The C is held underneath through the walking episode and into the falling scales.
transitions.evidence: Mutopia score, III, bars 21–50; the dominant pedal and walking episode are described at https://www.teoria.com/en/articles/2022/vivaldi-seasons/inverno/03.php.

transitions.title: Descending scales to the F minor solo
transitions.from: B · Strings over C, descending figures
transitions.to: C · Solo semiquavers over held strings
transitions.how: The strings play descending scales, and the soloist then starts a running passage from F. Its detached semiquavers climb above held notes in the upper strings. The basso rests for a few bars. The solo modulates from F minor towards C minor, and long pedals on C and G support the later part of the passage.
transitions.evidence: Mutopia score, III, bars 48–84; harmonic route at https://www.teoria.com/en/articles/2022/vivaldi-seasons/inverno/03.php.

transitions.title: Tutti in C minor after solo triplets
transitions.from: C · Solo semiquavers over held strings
transitions.to: D · Short string phrases, C minor
transitions.how: The solo’s descending triplets lead to a tutti in C minor. The running scales are broken into short notes, rests and brief demisemiquaver flurries. The exchanges are held over G, the dominant, and the solo ends the passage on a low G.
transitions.evidence: Mutopia score, III, bars 80–100: https://www.mutopiaproject.org/cgibin/piece-info.cgi?id=351; C-minor context described by Rodríguez Alvira.

transitions.title: The basso drops out in E♭
transitions.from: D · Short string phrases, C minor
transitions.to: E · Lento, E♭ major, without basses
transitions.how: The C-minor solo ends on G. At the Lento the upper strings begin in E♭ major, and the basso is silent for nineteen bars. The violin’s opening G–F–E♭ is now played in quavers under the words Il Vento Sirocco.
transitions.evidence: Mutopia score, III, bars 100–119; E♭ major identified at https://www.teoria.com/en/articles/2022/vivaldi-seasons/inverno/03.php.

transitions.title: Solo demisemiquavers on E♭
transitions.from: E · Lento, E♭ major, without basses
transitions.to: F · Solo runs and repeated-note tutti
transitions.how: The solo violin enters with demisemiquavers on E♭, under the words naming Boreas and all the winds. Tutti passages in repeated notes interrupt its runs, and the bass returns with them. The episode moves from E♭ major to F minor.
transitions.evidence: Mutopia score, III, bars 120–139; harmonic route described at https://www.teoria.com/en/articles/2022/vivaldi-seasons/inverno/03.php.

transitions.title: Soloist and strings in the final tutti
transitions.from: F · Solo runs and repeated-note tutti
transitions.to: F′ · Wind figures in F minor
transitions.how: The soloist rejoins the full strings in F minor. All play repeated demisemiquavers and downward runs, which continue the wind music through the final tutti (bars 137–153). E♮ sharpens the approach to F before the last held chord.
transitions.evidence: Mutopia score, III, closing tutti, bars 137–153: https://www.mutopiaproject.org/cgibin/piece-info.cgi?id=351.

source.title: Vivaldi, The Four Seasons — Mutopia score after Performers’ Facsimiles
source.locator: III. Allegro; solo opening, basso pedals, bars 101–119 basso tacet, and final wind episodes. Passage-level participation, not individual attack alignment; cellos/basses represent the written basso part, with no claim about keyboard realization.

timeline.note: The solo violin moves over the long F bass; orchestral upper strings rest.
Upper strings join over the held dominant C.
Running solo over sustained upper-string support; the basso briefly rests.
Low pedal support resumes beneath the continuing solo passage.
Tutti interruptions and a solo link alternate in this passage.
The Sirocco Lento removes the basso for nineteen bars.
Rapid solo figures alternate with short orchestral wind bursts; the orchestra plays intermittently.
The full-string wind figures drive the conclusion.

voices: Organ and cello bass line (not realised continuo)

composer.epithet: Venetian composer of concertos for the women of the Pietà and operas for the city’s theatres, who wrote a barking dog for the viola.
facts: Violin with his father Giovanni Battista, a player at St Mark’s, Venice
Pietà violin teacher from 1703; maestro de’ concerti from 1716; court service in Mantua, 1718–20
More than 500 concertos, operas, sacred music and sonatas
composer.background:
In 1703 Antonio Vivaldi, a twenty-five-year-old Venetian, was ordained priest in March and became a violin teacher in September. He had red hair, a formidable bow arm and a chest complaint that made celebrating Mass difficult. His father Giovanni Battista had been a barber before joining the violinists at St Mark’s; he taught Antonio and went on helping with his career long after the son had become famous. In Venice Antonio was known as il prete rosso, the red priest. He worked in the chapel, the orchestra gallery and the opera house.

The Ospedale della Pietà cared for abandoned children. Its musical establishment was a selected group of girls and women, trained to sing and play to a standard that brought visitors from across Europe. Some remained there as adult musicians and teachers. Vivaldi taught the advanced string players, rehearsed the orchestra and supplied new pieces. The governors voted on his employment each year. In 1709 they dispensed with him, and in 1711 they took him back.
